newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST - CPI figures set to boost Iberian bonds.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - CPI figures set to boost Iberian bonds.

text.p: Iberian fixed rate bonds should benefit from good inflation news in Spain and Portugal next week which will open the way to a further rate cut in Spain, analysts said.
The Bank of Portugal, clearly anticipating good news on the prices' front, beat Spain's central bank to the punch on Friday by cutting its repurchase pact rate by 30 basis points to 6.0 percent.

The 10-year cash spread between both markets and the German Bund could narrow slightly, but only slightly, because of the approach of the May 20 U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, they added.

The Spanish yield curve is already largely discounting a 25 basis point cut in the repo rate there to 5.25 percent on May 16. Analysts said that it would take a cut of 50 basis points to steepen the curve.
According to a Reuter poll, Spain's year-on-year inflation rate for April, due to be released on May 14, will be between 1.7 and 1.9 percent against 2.2 percent in March.
In Portugal, where the figures must be issued by May 15, a similar poll showed most analysts expecting a year-on-year rate of around 1.8 percent, down from 2.5 percent in March.

"We expect the CPI (consumer price index) to fall from 2.2 percent to 1.9 percent and that the Bank of Spain cuts the repo to 5.25 percent on May 16," said analyst Valentin Fernandez of Credit Lyonnais in Madrid.

Bank of America analyst Henrik Lumholdt said that the spread between the 10-year cash Bono and the Bund could break below 90 basis points, from the current 91, but it would be difficult to break through 85 basis points.
"Brussels is going to approve (Spain and Portugal's) convergence plans and the spreads with the Bunds can fall a little but they are already near the minimums," said a London fixed income trader.
"We still have the Fed and the elections in France could cause some turbulence in the currency markets," he added.
"88 basis points (between the Bono and the Bund) already discounts an 85 percent probability of Spain being in the euro in 1999," said Fernandez, referring to the launch of the single currency.
Analysts expected the spread between the Portuguese 10-year bonds (OT) and the Bonos to remain at between a negative five and 10 basis points.
The spreads with the Bunds hit record lows of 83 basis points for Spain and 80 for Portugal at the end of January.
